note: Private mutation/regression corpus for SwiftProjectLint (a SwiftPM monorepo — rules live under Packages/*). Mutants live in a detector's own source; each is killed by the root package's CoreTests. Run via `swift test --filter`. Not a scored benchmark. Two shapes: the ExtractableTotalKernelVisitor (the §15.2.5 'lift the trapped kernel' rule) and the ComputedPropertyViewVisitor's gates.

mutants.label: isWorthExtracting's `governs` is forced false — a genuine chunking kernel is never surfaced
the purity guard is inverted — the rule scans pure functions (which ARE the kernel) instead of the impure methods that trap one
isWorthExtracting returns true unconditionally — merely-stored arithmetic (assigned, not governing) is falsely flagged
the ambient-state guard is removed — a clock read (`ContinuousClock.now - lastActivityAt`) is reported as a kernel that 'depends only on its parameters and locals'
the toolbar names are dropped from decomposingContainers — the rule again advises wrapping a ToolbarItemGroup's two buttons in one View struct, which places one toolbar item where there were two
reachesHiddenMember always returns false — a property forwarding to a sibling declared in another file reads as depending on nothing, which is the strongest possible pass of the narrowing gate
hiddenMembers stops subtracting the extensions in the file under analysis — every type with a same-file extension goes silent, an over-gate introduced by the fix for an under-gate
the pre-scan's clean-instance-method catalog is built and then never assigned to the per-file detector — the linter reports fewer property-test candidates, correctly formatted, with no error anywhere
the AppKit/UIKit prefix set grows to every Apple two-letter prefix — CLIToolCommandRunner begins CL + uppercase and goes silent for a reason unrelated to why it should be silent

the closure-wrapper collector counts computed properties as storage — `var now: Date { make() }` is the wrapper's whole point, so every real instance stops qualifying and the exemption reaches nothing

the pure-kernel storage test becomes a denylist (only unreadable spellings disqualify) — the first implementation, which exempted a type storing UserDefaults and one storing a SwiftData ModelContainer
SelfAccessAnalyzer collects key-path component names again — `rules.filter(\.value.enabled)` reads as `self.value` and refuses the method, and through the clean-method catalog every caller
the key-path skip is widened to everything under a KeyPathExprSyntax — `rows.map(\.[index])` stops reading `index`, so a method reading mutable state through a subscript component is admitted
BooleanControlCoupling skips only member names again, not key-path components — `rules.contains(where: \.verbose)` reads as a branch on the `verbose` parameter and is reported as control coupling
ActorReentrancy's condition scan matches any name again — `guard !jobs.contains(where: \.isLoading)` and `guard !job.isLoading` read as checks of the actor's own `isLoading` and are reported
ActorReentrancy's await-operand scan matches any name again — `await send(jobs.map(\.isLoading))` reads as consuming the actor's `isLoading`, and a genuine unguarded `guard !isLoading` is dropped

ComputedPropertyView counts every DeclReferenceExpr as a dependency again — `List(messages, id: \.title)` reads as depending on the view's `title`, so the property seems to read every input and is never reported
NonInjectedNondeterminism counts a key-path component as a use of the local binding again — `let id = UUID(); Order(id: id, lineIDs: lines.map(\.id))` loses the composition-root message
VariableShadowing's rebinding check matches any identifier token again — `let total = orders.map(\.total).reduce(0, +)` passes as a rebinding of `total` and the shadow goes unreported
CatchWithoutHandling counts any `error` spelling as the caught error again — `filter(\.error)`, `result.error` and `self.error = nil` read as handling it, and the swallowing catch is not reported
URLSessionUnhandledError counts any `error` spelling as the parameter again — `decode(data).filter(\.error)` reads as checking the request's error, and the unchecked handler is not reported
ImpureCallInViewBody matches a marker's spelling anywhere again — `jobs.filter(\.print)` and `doc.print` in a view body are reported as calls to `print`
IOS17ObservationMigration takes any `$` prefix for a projected value again — `items.reduce(0) { $0 + $1 }` reads as Combine use and a plain @Published store gets no migration suggestion

the shared isMemberNameOfOtherBase treats `self` as another base — the over-correction: `self.connection` stops counting as the actor's property in an await operand, and a resource guard `guard connection != nil` is reported

Actor Reentrancy counts another value's member in an await operand as the actor's property — `await send(job.isLoading)` marks `isLoading` as a consumed resource and a genuine `guard !isLoading` is dropped
isMemberNameOfOtherBase does not see through parentheses — `guard !(self).isLoading` stops being the actor's gate

Catch Without Handling reads only `error` — `catch let e as DecodingError { self.lastError = e }` and `catch AppError.invalid(let message) { status = message }` are reported though they use what was caught
Catch Without Handling counts an implicit member spelled `error` as the caught error — `catch { state = .error }` looks handled
Variable Shadowing does not read a capture list — `let handler = { [handler] in … }` captures the outer `handler` and is reported as a shadow

ProjectLinter builds the package purity and binds .unconfigured instead — every oracle in the run judges each declaration alone again, and the linter reports more candidates, correctly formatted, with no error anywhere

the pre-scan is hoisted above the binding — the clean-method catalog and the one-hop join are built by unconfigured oracles while the per-file rules judge with the facts, so one run disagrees with itself
isProductionSource admits every path — a test target's `struct Item { let id = UUID() }` refutes a production `Item(n:)` it is not

PackagePurity.build no longer puts the universe in ConstructionUniverse.buildOrder — SEI reports the first of two declarations' witnesses in input order, so the message depends on the order the file system enumerates
the universe walk follows include_nested_packages — a type declared in a nested local package is invisible by default, so constructing it from the root reads as pure

per-file analysis parses its own copy instead of judging the shared tree — SEI types an assignment target by node identity, so on a re-parse an assignment to a property declared twice under #if is typed by both declarations and refutes

universePath classifies a symlinked file at its target again whenever the target is inside the root — Sources/Lib/Item.swift linking to Tests/Shared/Item.swift is read as a test file and dropped, so constructing the Item SwiftPM compiles into Lib reads as pure

the universe drops the nested-package bound and takes every nested package — an unrelated Demo/ package's refuting Row refutes the app's own plain Row(n:), withdraws two candidates and takes ReportBuilder's pure-kernel exemption, so Direct Instantiation warns and the default CLI exits 1

with include_nested_packages on, the universe reuses the reportable list instead of the walk the run already made without exclusions — an excluded directory's and a generated file's types drop out of the table, and constructing them reads as pure, only when nested packages are reported

two universe entries that are one file on disk keep the first one discovery returned rather than the smallest path, so which spelling SEI reads — and the witness it reports — depends on the file system's listing order, and differs from SwiftInferProperties'

constructionSources collapses a file's entries before classifying them — AppTests/Item.swift, a link to Sources/Lib/Item.swift, is the smaller path, stands for the file, and is then dropped as a test file, taking the Item SwiftPM compiles into Lib out of the table
compiledByRoot places a symlinked file in the package its target sits in — Sources/Lib/Item.swift linking into an uncompiled Demo/ leaves with Demo, though SwiftPM compiles it into Lib

ConstructionUniverse.buildOrder sorts by path component rather than with String < — Sources/A-B/X.swift and Sources/A/X.swift swap, so SEI reads one name's declarations in another order than SwiftInferProperties and can report another witness

any existing entry named Package.swift makes a package boundary again (amendment F) — a source file of that name in Sources/App/Models/ takes every file beside it out of the universe, so building the Item SwiftPM compiles into App reads as pure
an .xcodeproj beside the root manifest no longer counts as doubt (amendment G) — the manifest's closure bounds the universe, and a local package only the Xcode app target links leaves the table

the manifest reader takes a path literal's source text instead of its value (amendment H) — .package(path: "Packages/\u{55}til") names no package, and the Util package the root compiles leaves the table

references and nested packages are matched by spelling rather than by canonical location (amendments H and Q) — a dependency through a link to the walked package's directory, through /tmp for /private/tmp, or in another letter case reaches nothing

the closure follows a dependency only into a directory the walk recorded as a package (amendment I) — a root depending on .support or Pods/Support, which depends on Shared, stops there, and Shared's types leave the table

a nested package the run reports on is no longer taken into the universe (amendment J) — with --include-nested-packages its own functions are judged without its own types, tokenCount is offered and TokenBuilder passes as a pure kernel
the bound's manifest reads run on the cooperative pool again (amendment K) — a dependency's Package.swift holding a 1,000-arm else if overflows the 512 KB stack and the run dies with SIGBUS
the file walk skips anything carrying macOS's UF_HIDDEN flag again (amendment M) — a flagged source SwiftPM compiles leaves the universe, and building its type reads as pure
the closure reads each directory's Package.swift and ignores its Package@swift-*.swift manifests (amendment O) — a dependency named only in Package@swift-6.0.swift leaves the table
the closure ignores target path: arguments (amendment P) — a root target whose sources lie in Core/ no longer reaches the Core package, and Core's types leave the table

isManifest looks for the tools-version comment on the very first line again, not the first non-blank one (amendment S a) — a dependency's manifest opening with a blank line is no manifest, passes nothing on, and the package behind it leaves the table

isManifest compares the swift-tools-version label case-sensitively on the first non-blank line (amendment S a) — `// SWIFT-TOOLS-VERSION:5.9`, which SwiftPM loads, is no manifest, and the closure stops there
isManifest drops the later-line clause (amendment S b) — a 6.0 manifest below a license header, which SwiftPM loads, is no manifest, and the package behind it leaves the table
a target path reaches only the nested packages that hold it again, not those under it (amendment T) — `.target(name: "All", path: "Packages")` compiles Packages/A's sources, yet A leaves the table

the target-path comparison loses its `location.isEmpty` clause (amendment T′) — a root target's `path: "."` resolves to the root, "", which no hasPrefix matches, so it reaches no nested package and Packages/A, whose sources that target compiles, leaves the table

isManifest's first-line test takes only spaces and tabs around the marker again (amendment 4b, S′) — `//\u{00A0}swift-tools-version:5.9`, which SwiftPM loads, is no manifest, so a dependency's closure is dropped or a root is left unbounded

the later-line prefilter compares the label without lowercasing it (amendment 4b, S′) — a 6.0 `// SWIFT-TOOLS-VERSION` below a header never reaches the case-insensitive regex, and the manifest SwiftPM loads is none
